title: Local Devbox LLM Proxy Manifest (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal sketch for a lightweight local devbox proxy that mirrors Redwood runtime behavior for iteration and debugging. Goal is not full parity but to reproduce routing, basic KV cache semantics, token accounting, and telemetry hooks developers expect when iterating offline or behind corporate VPNs.

Constraints / assumptions:
- Runs on developer machine (mac/linux). Prefer single binary or simple docker compose.
- Should be able to stand in for Redwood Hosted or Redwood Dedicated endpoints for dev flows (feature flags, model routing emulation).
- Not a secure production path; hides behind local auth (unix socket / local API key).
- Must emit compatible telemetry envelopes to local collector so SREs and DX can replay traces.

High-level components:
- devbox-cli: local shim for dev commands (wraps openai/redwood CLI calls).
- dev-proxy: HTTP/Unix-socket service that accepts Redwood API shapes (subset) and routes to: local-model (optional), remote-hosted (when online), or stubbed-variants.
- local-model-adapter: small gRPC/HTTP adapter for running tiny open models (ggml etc.) or dockerized runtime.
- kv-cache-store: file-backed KV cache emulator (prefix cache semantics).
- telemetry-forwarder: emits same envelope structure but writes to local file or forwards to staging telemetry endpoint.

ASCII diagram (conceptual):

  +------------+     +-----------+    +--------------------+
  | devbox-cli | <-- | dev-proxy | -> | local-model-adapter | (optional)
  +------------+     +-----------+    +--------------------+
                              |
                              v
                      +----------------+
                      | kv-cache-store |
                      +----------------+
                              |
                              v
                    +---------------------+
                    | telemetry-forwarder | -> local telemetry file / staging
                    +---------------------+

Core API surface to support (subset of Redwood API):
- POST /v1/generate  (body: {model, prompt, max_tokens, streaming: bool, meta})
- POST /v1/chat      (body: {model, messages[], system, streaming})
- POST /v1/embeddings (body: {model, input[]})
- GET  /v1/models    (list model variants available locally/stubbed)
- POST /v1/kv/query  (body: {cache_key, prefix_hint})  -> returns cached tokens/fragment if hit
- POST /v1/debug/trace (body: {trace_id, span})  -> local trace ingestion endpoint

Example HTTP request/response shape (generate):
Request JSON (client):
{
  "model": "redwood-dummy-1",
  "prompt": "Summarize this file: ...",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "streaming": false,
  "meta": {"devbox":true, "feature_flag":"local-routing"}
}
Response JSON (proxy) success:
{
  "id": "gen_01F...",
  "model": "redwood-dummy-1",
  "tokens_used": 48,
  "result": "Concise summary...",
  "cache_hit": false,
  "route": "local-model-adapter"
}

Config manifest (sketch, YAML-like but stored as small JSON file under ~/.devbox-proxy/manifest.json):
- name: devbox-local-proxy
  version: 0.1.0
  listen: unix:///tmp/devbox-redwood.sock  # or http://127.0.0.1:4600
  auth: { type: local-key, key_path: ~/.devbox-proxy/key }
  routing:
    - match: { model_prefix: "redwood-" }
      action: local if local_model_available else remote("https://api.redwood.ai")
    - match: { kind: embeddings }
      action: remote("https://api.redwood.ai/embeddings")
  cache:
    enabled: true
    path: ~/.devbox-proxy/cache.db  # sqlite file keyed by prompt-hash
    ttl_seconds: 3600
  telemetry:
    forward_to: file://~/.devbox-proxy/telemetry.log
    sample_rate: 0.05
  model_adapters:
    local_model_adapters:
      - name: ggml-7b-lite
        cmd: ["/usr/local/bin/ggml-runner", "--socket", "/tmp/ggml.sock"]

Telemetry envelope (local-file format, one JSON per line):
{
  "trace_id": "t-01E...",
  "time": "2026-03-04T14:12:03Z",
  "route": "local-model-adapter",
  "latency_ms": 210,
  "tokens_in": 56,
  "tokens_out": 42,
  "cache_hit": false,
  "devbox_user": "maya",
  "session_id": "s-123"
}

KV cache semantics (notes):
- key: deterministic hash of normalized prompt (strip ephemeral meta like timestamps).
- store: small sqlite map {key, model, value_blob, created_at, ttl_seconds}.
- prefix hits: if request includes prefix_hint the proxy may serve partial tokenized sequences (used in prefix/KV caching experiments). Emulate Redwood behavior: prefer exact full-key hit, then prefix fallback (if allowed by config).

Routing emulator details:
- Rule engine is intentionally simple (ordered list). Each rule has matchers (model_prefix, tag, kind, size_hint). First matching rule wins. Rules can reference local adapters or remote endpoints with a failsafe fallback-timeout.
- When forwarding to remote, attach X-Devbox-Trace header to distinguish dev traffic.

Compatibility & parity gaps (things we won't emulate initially):
- true batching behavior & continuous batching kernels (we'll approximate by single-request passthrough).
- GPU optimized runtime kernels and quantized execution timing.
- Complex rollout policies (but can stub route metadata).

Developer UX flows:
1) Start dev-proxy via devbox-cli: `devbox start` -> launches socket and adapters.
2) Set environment: `export REDWOOD_API_URL=unix:///tmp/devbox-redwood.sock`
3) Run tests or interactive REPL. Telemetry written locally for later upload via `devbox upload-telemetry --target staging`

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical local auth model (unix-socket + optional token). Edge-case: dockerized dev flows need HTTP and API key.
- Do we allow automatic fallback to real remote when offline vs explicit `force-local` flag? Risk: accidental remote calls and leaking data.
- How closely should the local KV prefix semantics match production? We need to avoid producing false-positive cache hits that mask production misses.
- UX: Should the proxy offer a `--record` mode to capture real remote traces and play them back locally? Very useful for reproducible debugging.
- Expose a small web UI to inspect cache and recent traces (low priority).

Next steps (practical):
- Prototype: small Go binary with net/http + unix socket, sqlite cache, and simple rule engine. 2 week spike.
- Minimal adapter: provide a docker-compose recipe to run ggml runtime as example.
- Draft README + quickstart with example workflows and CI integration for local integration tests.

Notes to self: keep manifest format intentionally tiny and migratable (JSON schema v1). Try to reuse telemetry envelope keys that the tracing infra expects (trace_id, span_id, latency_ms). When in doubt, make the format verbose and map to production fields later.

References and related tickets: ENG-1289 (dev-proxy umbrella), PR: github.com/redwood-inference/devbox-proxy#42, confluence:Devbox-Local-Proxy-Notes

End of sketch.
